hypothesis: Unmapped faults in the footprint are most likely to occur in structural gaps within the visible fault network. Network-aware context features that describe each pixel's position relative to the visible catalogue (fault density, junction proximity, structural gap features, fault segment length, distance-to-network bins, strike coherence and variability) will raise the kernel credit per emitted dot on withheld fault segments, beyond what orientation-steered derivative filters alone can achieve (H78-A). The catalogue's location is NOT exposed to the learner; only its orientation and network topology are used, so the model is not paid to crowd known traces.

shared_tools_unmodified.source: buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE77 vendor/gems57 (pinned in its registry/template_pin.json to 60GEMSDOE b99591ee)

holdout.scoring: pooled DTI alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 triangular 300 m; 95% CI paired 20 km block bootstrap (1000 draws, seed 520810)
holdout.training: one model per arm on ALL visible catalogue cells (deployment-faithful); negatives sampled > 2 px from visible cells; withheld cells NOT excluded from training (they are masked in evaluation but the model sees them as negatives)
holdout.catalogue_derived_inputs: strike field from visible cells (orientation only, no location); network context features: fault density, junction proximity, structural gap features, segment length, distance bins (categorical, no raw distance), strike coherence/variability - ALL computed from visible catalogue only

arms.A1_iso: A0 + rotation-invariant Hessian eigenvalues and gradient magnitude at sigma 1.5/3 px on 6 bands
arms.A3_h78_net: A2 + network context features: fault density, junction proximity, across/along-strike gap features, segment length, distance-to-network bins (7 categories), strike coherence, strike energy, strike variability (CANDIDATE)

emitter: greedy max-score packing, min separation 2.8 px (allows sqrt(8)), visible-catalogue flank <= 3 px excluded; budgets 25k-60k; A3 variants: flank 0/2/3 px, ridge-NMS on/off
canary: single-feature AUC on withheld truth vs active background; > 0.90 = leakage until proven otherwise
uniqueness_rule: Spearman rho vs any registry raster <= 0.90 on the footprint AND fraction of final dots within 3 px of any registry dot set <= 0.70; checked on the score surface before placement AND on the final dots

decision_rules.hypothesis_supported: best A3 config pooled HOLDOUT-DTI > matched A2 config AND paired-bootstrap 95% CI of the difference excludes 0
decision_rules.ok_to_submit: best A3 config pooled HOLDOUT-DTI > matched A0 (lineage base) and > matched A2 (steered) with CI lower bound > 0 AND canary clean AND uniqueness pass AND validator pass (single band float32, 3730x3292, EPSG:32611, transform (100,0,243350,0,-100,4508550), all finite, values in [0,1], no NaN inside footprint, zero positives on the catalogue)
decision_rules.negative: anything else; the file is still built and published for inspection, labelled NOT OK TO SUBMIT

budget: 3 experiments: E1 arms+canary (run_holdout_net.py), E2 emission sweep (same run), E3 final build + uniqueness + validator (build_submission_net.py); stop afterwards
what_this_cannot_show: A catalogue hide-and-recover holdout measures recovery of withheld mapped faults; it is not an organizer score and never a leaderboard projection. The holdout draw removes every visible catalogue cell within 3 px of a withheld component, so by construction no withheld truth lies within 3 px of a visible fault - the 3-px flank prune therefore cannot remove dots that sit on holdout truth, which may bias the holdout in favour of larger flank radii.

network_features_detail.leakage_safety: All features derived from visible catalogue only. No raw distance values exposed (only binned categories). No hidden truth information used. Distance bins are one-hot encoded to prevent ordinal leakage.
network_features_detail.computation: All network features computed at sigma_region=40px (4km) scale, matching the strike field computation.
